nodes.name: Schrodinger junction
nodes.statement:
Our investigation covers all point-like defects in the vertex, 
which are compatible with a unitary time evolution in the bulk generated by the Schr\"odinger Hamiltonian. We call 
these systems Schr\"odinger junctions.

nodes.name: Star graph coordinates
nodes.statement:
The system in Fig. \ref{fig1} is localised on a star graph 
with coordinates $\{(x,i)\, ,:\, x\leq 0,\, i=1,...,N\}$, where $x$ denotes 
the distance from the vertex and $i$ labels the leads.
nodes.section: 2.1 Particle current in the presence of defect

nodes.name: Particle current j(t,x,i)
nodes.statement:
The main 
object of our investigation is the particle current $j(t,x,i)$ flowing along the 
leads of the junction.
nodes.section: 2.1 Particle current in the presence of defect

nodes.name: Bulk dynamics and vertex boundary condition
nodes.section: 2.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.statement_short: Free Schrodinger equation on the leads with a vertex boundary condition fixed by a unitary matrix U and a mass scale eta.

nodes.name: Schrodinger equation on the leads
nodes.statement: \left ({\rm i} {\partial}_t +\frac{1}{2m} {\partial}_x^2\right )\psi (t,x,i) = 0\, ,
nodes.section: 2.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.label: eqm1

nodes.name: Vertex boundary condition
nodes.statement: \lim_{x\to 0^-}\sum_{j=1}^N \left [\eta (\mbox{${\mathbb I}$}-\mathbb U)_{ij} +{\rm i} (\mbox{${\mathbb I}$}+\mathbb U)_{ij}{\partial}_x \right ] \psi (t,x,j) = 0\, ,
nodes.section: 2.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.label: bc1

nodes.name: Scattering matrix of a point-like defect
nodes.section: 2.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.statement_short: The boundary condition parametrises all self-adjoint extensions and yields the scattering matrix S(k) in terms of U and eta.

nodes.name: Scattering matrix of the point-like defect
nodes.statement: \mathbb S(k) = -\frac{[\eta (\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} - \mathbb U) - k(\mbox{${\mathbb I}$}+\mathbb U )]}{[\eta (\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} - \mathbb U) + k(\mbox{${\mathbb I}$}+\mathbb U)]} \, ,
nodes.section: 2.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.label: S1

nodes.name: Solution of the boundary value problem
nodes.section: 2.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.statement_short: Mode expansion of the field psi in terms of scattering waves chi and CAR generators a_j(k).

nodes.name: Solution field psi
nodes.statement: \psi (t,x,i) = \sum_{j=1}^N \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{dk}{2\pi } {\rm e}^{-{\rm i} \omega (k)t}\, \chi_{ij}(k;x) a_j (k) \, , \qquad \omega(k) = \frac {k^2}{2m} \, .
nodes.section: 2.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.label: psi1

nodes.name: Scattering wave functions chi
nodes.statement: \chi(k;x) = {\rm e}^{-{\rm i} k x}\, \mbox{${\mathbb I}$} + {\rm e}^{{\rm i} k x}\, \mathbb S(-k)
nodes.section: 2.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.label: chi

nodes.name: Particle current operator
nodes.section: 2.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.statement_short: Bilinear expression of the particle current j(t,x,i) in the oscillators a, a*.

nodes.name: Particle current operator
nodes.statement: j(t,x,i)= \frac{{\rm i}}{2m} \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} k}{2\pi} \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} p}{2\pi}\, {\rm e}^{{\rm i} t [\omega(k) - \omega(p)]} \qquad \qquad \qquad \nonumber \\ \times \sum_{l,m=1}^N a^*_l(k) \Bigl \{ \chi^*_{li}(k;x) \left [\partial_{x} \chi_{i m}\right ](p;x) - \left [\partial_{x} \chi^*_{li}\right ](k;x) \chi_{im}(p;x) \Bigr \}a_m(p) \, .
nodes.section: 2.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.label: curr1

nodes.name: Operator Kirchhoff rule
nodes.section: 2.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.statement_short: The currents at the vertex sum to zero over all leads.
nodes.label: KR

nodes.name: Landauer-Buttiker non-equilibrium steady state
nodes.statement:
The physical setting, presented in 
Fig. \ref{fig1}, is nicely described by the Landauer-B\"uttiker (LB) \cite{L-57, B-86} 
non-equilibrium steady state $\Omega_{\beta, \mu}$, defined in terms of 
$(\beta_i,\mu_i)$ and $\mathbb S(k)$. A simple and intuitive way \cite{M-11} to 
construct this state is to use the scattering matrix $\mathbb S(k)$ in order to 
extend the tensor product of Gibbs states, relative to the 
reservoirs $R_i$ at the level of asymptotic incoming fields, to the outgoing fields.
nodes.section: 2.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.statement_short: The LB steady state extends the product of reservoir Gibbs states from incoming to outgoing fields via S(k).

nodes.name: n-point current correlation function
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state

nodes.name: n-point current correlation function
nodes.statement: {\mathcal W}^i_n(t_1, x_1,...,t_n,x_n) = \langle j(t_1,x_1,i) \cdots j(t_n,x_n,i) \rangle_{\beta,\mu}\, ,
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: w1

nodes.name: n-th current cumulant
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state

nodes.name: n-th current cumulant
nodes.statement: \mathcal C^i_n(t_1, x_1,...,t_n,x_n) = \langle j(t_1,x_1,i) \cdots j(t_n,x_n,i) \rangle_{\beta,\mu}^{\rm conn}\, .
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: c1

nodes.name: Landauer-Buttiker current (first cumulant)
nodes.statement: {\mathcal W}^i_1 = \mathcal C^i_1 = \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi} \sum_{l=1}^N \left (\delta_{il} -|\mathbb S_{il}(\sqrt{2m\omega})|^2\right ) d_l(\omega) \, , \qquad d_l(\omega)= \frac{1}{1+{\rm e}^{\beta_l (\omega -\mu_l)}}\, .
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: c11

nodes.name: Time differences
nodes.statement:
First of all the 
correlators (\ref{w1},\ref{c1}) depend on the time differences 
$\{\hat{t}_k \equiv t_k - t_{k+1}\, :\, k=1,...,n-1\}$, which reflects 
the invariance under time translations of the LB state.
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state

nodes.name: Time-integrated current replacement
nodes.statement: j(t_l,x_l,i) \longmapsto \int_0^T {\rm d} t_l \, j(t_l,x_l,i) \, , \qquad \forall \; l=1,...n\, ,
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: c2

nodes.name: Zero-frequency correlators
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.statement_short: Fourier transform of the n-point correlators in the time differences, followed by the zero-frequency limit.

nodes.name: Fourier transform of correlators
nodes.statement: \mathcal Z^i_n(x_1,...,x_n;\nu ) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} {\rm d} \hat{t}_1 \cdots \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} {\rm d} \hat{t}_{n-1} {\rm e}^{{\rm i} \nu (\hat{t}_1+\cdots \hat{t}_{n-1})} \mathcal Z^i_n(t_1, x_1,...,t_n,x_n)\, , \qquad \mathcal Z^i_n = {\mathcal W}^i_n,\, \mathcal C^i_n\, ,
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: c3

nodes.name: Zero-frequency limit
nodes.statement: \mathcal Z^i_n = \lim_{\nu \to 0^+} \mathcal Z^i_n(x_1,...,x_n;\nu ) \, .
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: c4

nodes.name: Determinant formula for W_n
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.statement_short: The zero-frequency n-point correlator is an energy integral of a determinant built from T-matrix entries and Fermi distributions.

nodes.name: Determinant formula for W_n
nodes.statement: {\mathcal W}^i_n=\int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi} \sum_{l_1,...,l_n=1}^N \left | \begin{array}{cccccccc} \mathbb T^i_{l_1l_1}(\omega)d_{l_1}(\omega )&\mathbb T^i_{l_2l_1}(\omega)d_{l_2}(\omega )&\cdots && \mathbb T^i_{l_nl_1}(\omega)d_{l_n}(\omega )\\ -\mathbb T^i_{l_1l_2}(\omega)\widetilde{d}_{l_1}(\omega )&\mathbb T^i_{l_2l_2}(\omega)d_{l_2}(\omega )& \cdots & &\mathbb T^i_{l_nl_2}(\omega)d_{l_n}(\omega )\\ \vdots &\vdots & \vdots&& \vdots \\ -\mathbb T^i_{l_1l_n}(\omega)\widetilde{d}_{l_1}(\omega )&-\mathbb T^i_{l_2l_n}(\omega)\widetilde{d}_{l_2}(\omega ) & \cdots & &\mathbb T^i_{l_nl_n}(\omega)d_{l_n}(\omega )\\ \end{array}\right | \, ,
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: w2

nodes.name: T-matrix
nodes.statement: \mathbb T^i_{lm}(\omega)=\delta_{li} \delta_{mi} - \mathbb S_{li}(\sqrt{2m\omega})\, \overline{\mathbb S}_{mi}(\sqrt{2m\omega})\, ,
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: T

nodes.name: Complementary Fermi distribution
nodes.statement: \widetilde{d}_l(\omega ) = 1-d_l(\omega)=\frac{{\rm e}^{\beta_l (\omega -\mu_l)}}{1+{\rm e}^{\beta_l (\omega -\mu_l)}}\, .
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: T1

nodes.name: Matrices A, B, D
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state

nodes.name: Matrices A, B, D
nodes.statement: {\mathbb A}^i \equiv \mathbb T^i \, {\mathbb D}\, ,\qquad {\mathbb B}^i \equiv \mathbb T^i\, (\mbox{${\mathbb I}$}-{\mathbb D})\, ,\qquad {\mathbb D} \equiv {\rm diag}[d_1(\omega),d_2(\omega),...,d_n(\omega)] \, .
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: m1

nodes.name: Trace representation of current cumulants
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.statement_short: Each cumulant C_n is an energy integral of a sum over permutations of traces of products of A, B and +-A matrices.

nodes.name: Trace formula for C_1
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_1^i &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi} {\rm Tr} \left [ {\mathbb A}^i \right ]\, ,
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: c51

nodes.name: Trace formula for C_n
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_n^i &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi} \sum_{\sigma \in {\cal P}_{n-1}} \, {\rm Tr} \left [ {\mathbb A}^i {\mathbb C}^i_{\sigma_1\sigma_2}\cdots {\mathbb C}^i_{\sigma_{n-2}\sigma_{n-1}}{\mathbb B}^i\right ]\, , \qquad n \geq 2\, ,
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: c52

nodes.name: Matrix C_sigma
nodes.statement: {\mathbb C}^i_{\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}} = \begin{cases} \, -{\mathbb A}^i \, , & \qquad \sigma_i < \sigma_{i+1}\, , \\ \quad {\mathbb B}^i \, , & \qquad \sigma_i > \sigma_{i+1}\, . \\ \end{cases}
nodes.section: 2.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: m2

nodes.name: Notation C_n for lead L_1
nodes.statement:
Without loss of generality we can concentrate on the the cumulants $\mathcal C_n^1$ in the 
lead $L_1$. For notational simplicity we omit here and in what follows the 
apex $1$ in $\mathcal C_n^1$.

nodes.name: Two-lead junction cumulants C_1 to C_6
nodes.statement:
By means of (\ref{c51})-(\ref{m2}) one gets 
\begin{eqnarray} 
\mathcal C_1 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau c_1\, , \\
\mathcal C_2 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau (c_2 -\tau c_1^2)\, , \\
\mathcal C_3 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau^2 c_1(1-3c_2+2\tau c_1^2) \, , \\
\mathcal C_4 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau^2[c_2 -3c_2^2+12\tau c_1^2c_2 - 
2\tau c_1^2(2+3\tau c_1^2)]\, , \\
\mathcal C_5 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau^3 c_1[1+30c_2^2 -15c_2(1+4\tau c_1^2) + 
4\tau c_1^2(5+6\tau c_1^2)]\, , \\
\mathcal C_6 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau^3 \{c_2[1+15c_2(2c_2-1)] - 2\tau c_1^2[8+15c_2(9c_2-5)] +
\nonumber \\
&+&120 \tau^2 c_1^4(3c_2-1) -120\tau^3 c_1^6\}\, , \end{eqnarray}
where the following combinations 
\begin{equation}
c_1(\omega)\equiv d_1(\omega)-d_2(\omega)\, \qquad 
c_2(\omega)\equiv d_1(\omega)+d_2(\omega)-2d_1(\omega)d_2(\omega)\, , \end{equation}
have been introduced for convenience.
nodes.statement_short: Explicit first six cumulants of the two-lead junction as energy integrals of polynomials in tau, c_1, c_2.

nodes.name: Equation (2.21)
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_1 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau c_1\, ,
nodes.label: ec1

nodes.name: Equation (2.22)
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_2 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau (c_2 -\tau c_1^2)\, ,
nodes.label: ec2

nodes.name: Equation (2.23)
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_3 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau^2 c_1(1-3c_2+2\tau c_1^2) \, ,
nodes.label: ec3

nodes.name: Equation (2.24)
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_4 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau^2[c_2 -3c_2^2+12\tau c_1^2c_2 - 2\tau c_1^2(2+3\tau c_1^2)]\, ,
nodes.label: ec4

nodes.name: Combinations c_1, c_2
nodes.statement: c_1(\omega)\equiv d_1(\omega)-d_2(\omega)\, \qquad c_2(\omega)\equiv d_1(\omega)+d_2(\omega)-2d_1(\omega)d_2(\omega)\, ,
nodes.label: dc

nodes.name: Transmission probability tau
nodes.statement_short: Two-lead transmission probability tau(omega)=|S_12|^2 in terms of eta_i = eta tan(alpha_i).

nodes.name: Transmission probability tau
nodes.statement: \tau(\omega) = |\mathbb S_{12}(\sqrt{2m\omega})|^2 = \frac{2m\omega (\eta_1-\eta_2)^2 \sin^2 (\theta)}{(2m\omega+\eta_1^2)(2m\omega+\eta_2^2)} \, , \qquad \theta \in [0,2\pi)\, ,
nodes.label: tr

nodes.name: Parameters eta_i
nodes.statement: \eta_i \equiv \eta\, {\rm tan} (\alpha_i)\, , \qquad \alpha_i \in [-\pi/2, \pi/2)\, ,
nodes.label: tr1

nodes.name: Ansatz for the generating function
nodes.statement:
Following the pioneering work of Khlus \cite{K-87}, Lesovik and Levitov \cite{L-89, LL-92}, we 
look for a generating function in the form 
\begin{equation}
\mathcal C (\lambda ) = \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, 
\ln \left [1+F_{12}(\tau,d_1,d_2)\left ({\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda f(\tau)}-1\right ) 
+ F_{21}(\tau,d_1,d_2)\left ({\rm e}^{-{\rm i} \lambda f(\tau)}-1\right )\right ] \, , \end{equation} 
where $F_{12}$, $F_{21}$ and $f$ are unknown functions.
nodes.statement_short: Look for C(lambda) as an energy integral of a log of a three-term expression with unknown F_12, F_21, f.

nodes.name: Ansatz for the cumulant generating function
nodes.statement: \mathcal C (\lambda ) = \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \ln \left [1+F_{12}(\tau,d_1,d_2)\left ({\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda f(\tau)}-1\right ) + F_{21}(\tau,d_1,d_2)\left ({\rm e}^{-{\rm i} \lambda f(\tau)}-1\right )\right ] \, ,
nodes.label: gf1

nodes.name: Cumulant generating function
Cumulants from generating function
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_n = (-{\rm i} \partial_\lambda)^n\, \mathcal C(\lambda ) \vert_{{}_{\lambda =0}}
nodes.label: gft2

nodes.name: Two-terminal cumulant generating function
nodes.statement_short: Two-terminal CGF: energy integral of ln{1 + i c_1 sqrt(tau) sin(lambda sqrt(tau)) + c_2[cos(lambda sqrt(tau))-1]}.

nodes.name: Solved ansatz functions F_12, F_21, f
nodes.statement: F_{12} = \frac{1}{2}(c_2 + c_1\sqrt{\tau})\, , \qquad F_{21} = \frac{1}{2}(c_2 - c_1\sqrt{\tau})\, , \qquad f=\sqrt{\tau}\, .
nodes.label: gft3

nodes.name: Two-terminal cumulant generating function
nodes.statement: \mathcal C (\lambda ) &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \ln \left [1+\frac{1}{2}(c_2+c_1\sqrt{\tau})\left ({\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda \sqrt{\tau}}-1\right ) + \frac{1}{2}(c_2-c_1\sqrt{\tau})\left ({\rm e}^{-{\rm i} \lambda \sqrt{\tau}}-1\right )\right ] \nonumber \\ &=&\int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \ln \left \{1+ {\rm i} c_1 \sqrt{\tau}\, \sin (\lambda \sqrt{\tau}) +c_2 \left [\cos (\lambda \sqrt{\tau})-1\right ] \right \} \, .
nodes.label: gf4

nodes.name: gf4 reproduces C_4 to C_6
nodes.statement:
One can easily check also that (\ref{gf4}) reproduces perfectly the cumulants 
$\mathcal C_4$, $\mathcal C_5$ and $\mathcal C_6$ as well and represents therefore a valid candidate for 
the final result in the case of two leads.

nodes.name: Independence of energy channels
nodes.statement:
The argument in what follows is based on the fact that the 
particle transport in our system can be separated 
in statistically independent processes with fixed energy.
conclusions:
the 
particle transport in our system can be separated 
in statistically independent processes with fixed energy

nodes.name: Proof of energy-channel independence
nodes.statement:
In fact, excitations with different energies 
propagate in the graph in Fig. \ref{fig1} in a fully independent way, because the only interaction, localised in the vertex,  
leaves the energy invariant (see (\ref{A7})).
nodes.statement_short: The vertex interaction conserves energy, so excitations of different energies propagate independently.

nodes.name: Total CGF as integral over energy channels
Energy-integrated generating function
nodes.statement: \mathcal C^i(\lambda ) = \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \mathcal C_\omega^i(\lambda )\, ,
nodes.label: tgf

nodes.name: Single-energy-channel current
nodes.statement_short: Restricting the current to energy omega gives a quadratic form in fermionic oscillators with the T-matrix.

nodes.name: Single-energy-channel measure
nodes.statement: {\rm d} k\, {\rm d} p \longmapsto {\rm d} k\, {\rm d} p\, (2\pi)^2\, \delta \left (\frac{k^2}{2m} - \omega \right ) \delta (k-p)\, ,
nodes.label: fe1

nodes.name: Single-channel current
nodes.statement: j_\omega^i = \sum_{l,m=1}^N a^*_l\, \mathbb T^i_{lm}(\sqrt{2m\omega})\, a_m \, ,
nodes.label: curr2

nodes.name: Fermionic oscillator algebra
nodes.statement: [a_i\, ,\, a_j^*]_+ = \delta_{ij}\, ,\qquad [a_i\, ,\, a_j]_+ = [a^*_i\, ,\, a_j^*]_+ = 0\, , \qquad \langle a^*_i a_j\rangle_{\beta,\mu} = \delta_{ij} d_j(\omega)\, .
nodes.label: alg

Single-channel generating function

nodes.name: Determinant formula for the single-channel counting function
nodes.statement:
The expectation value $\langle {\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda j_w^i} \rangle_{\beta,\mu}$ 
can be evaluated explicitly. The key points of the computation, which leads to the final result 
\begin{equation}
\langle {\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda j_w^i} \rangle_{\beta,\mu} = {\rm det} \left [\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} + 
\left ({\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda \mathbb T^i(\sqrt{2m\omega})} -\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} \right ) {\mathbb D}(\omega) \right ]\, ,   \qquad   
{\mathbb D}(\omega ) \equiv {\rm diag}[d_1(\omega),d_2(\omega),...,d_n(\omega)] \, , \end{equation} 
are given appendix C.

nodes.statement_short: The N-terminal CGF has the two-terminal form with total transmission tau and an effective Fermi distribution for the other reservoirs.

nodes.statement: \tau(\omega) = \sum_{i=2}^N \tau_i (\omega)\, , \qquad \tau_i (\omega) \equiv |\mathbb S_{1i}(\sqrt{2m\omega})|^2 \, ,

nodes.statement:
As expected,  
the expression (\ref{gf6}) reproduces (\ref{gf4}) for $N=2$.

nodes.name: Scale-invariant cumulant generating function
nodes.statement_short: For critical S-matrices and equal temperatures the two-terminal CGF is a closed combination of dilogarithms.

nodes.name: Variables gamma_j and Lambda
nodes.statement: \gamma_j\equiv{\rm e}^{-\beta\mu_j}\, ,\qquad \Lambda(\lambda ) \equiv {\rm i} \sqrt{\tau}(\gamma_2-\gamma_1)\sin(\lambda\sqrt{\tau}) +(\gamma_2+\gamma_1)\cos(\lambda\sqrt{\tau})\, ,
nodes.label: si2

nodes.name: Scale-invariant generating function (dilogarithms)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \mathcal C(\lambda) = \frac{1}{2\pi \beta}\Bigg\{ &{\rm Li}_2\left (-\gamma_1^{-1}\right ) + {\rm Li}_2\left (-\gamma_2^{-1}\right ) \\ -&{\rm Li}_2\left[\frac{-2}{\Lambda(\lambda) - \sqrt{\Lambda^2(\lambda)-4\gamma_1\gamma_2}}\right] - {\rm Li}_2\left[\frac{-2}{\Lambda(\lambda) + \sqrt{\Lambda^2(\lambda)-4\gamma_1\gamma_2}}\right] \Bigg\}\, , \end{split}

nodes.name: Variables mu_+ and mu_-
Zero-temperature CGF at mu_+=0
nodes.statement:
For $\mu_+=0$ 
the expression (\ref{si3}) greatly simplifies 
in the low temperature limit $\beta \to \infty$. In fact, one finds 
\begin{equation}
\lim_{\beta \to \infty} \mathcal C (\lambda )\vert_{{}_{\mu_+=0}}  = 
\frac{|\mu_-|}{2\pi} \ln \left [\cos (\lambda \sqrt{\tau})
+ {\rm i}\, \varepsilon (\mu_-)\sqrt{\tau} \sin (\lambda \sqrt{\tau})\right ] \, , \end{equation} 
$\varepsilon$ being the sign function.

nodes.name: Zero-temperature generating function at mu_+=0
nodes.statement: \lim_{\beta \to \infty} \mathcal C (\lambda )\vert_{{}_{\mu_+=0}} = \frac{|\mu_-|}{2\pi} \ln \left [\cos (\lambda \sqrt{\tau}) + {\rm i}\, \varepsilon (\mu_-)\sqrt{\tau} \sin (\lambda \sqrt{\tau})\right ] \, ,
nodes.label: si4

nodes.name: Agreement with Levitov-Lesovik
nodes.statement:
The result (\ref{si4}) was derived for $\mu_->0$ independently 
by Levitov and Lesovik \cite{LL-92, LS-14} and provides therefore a valuable check 
on (\ref{si3}).

nodes.name: First four zero-temperature cumulants
First four cumulants at zero temperature
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_1 = \frac{\tau \mu_-}{2\pi} \, ,\qquad \mathcal C_2 = \frac{\tau (1-\tau)|\mu_-|}{2\pi}\, ,\qquad \mathcal C_3 = \frac{\tau^2(\tau-1) \mu_-}{\pi}\, ,\qquad \mathcal C_4 = \frac{ \tau^2(\tau-1)(1-3\tau) |\mu_-|}{\pi}\, .
nodes.label: si5

nodes.name: Odd cumulants proportional to the current
Odd cumulants proportional to current
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_{2n+1}\propto \mathcal C_1\, , \qquad \mu_+=0\, , \quad \beta \to \infty\, ,
nodes.label: prop

nodes.name: Transferred charge
Transferred charge
nodes.statement: Q_T = \int_0^T {\rm d} t\, \langle j(t,x,i)\rangle_{\beta,\mu} = T \mathcal C_1\, .
nodes.label: si6

nodes.name: Effective charge
Effective charge
nodes.statement: Q_T = \frac{ e^2\tau}{2\pi} VT = \frac{ e_{\rm eff}^2}{2\pi} VT\, , \qquad e_{\rm eff}\equiv e \sqrt {\tau}\, ,
nodes.label: si7

nodes.name: Charge renormalisation by the defect
nodes.statement:
We see that switching on the defect ($\tau < 1$) causes a finite 
renormalisation of the charge $e \longmapsto e_{\rm eff}$ 
with respect to the case in which the defect is absent ($\tau=1$). 
This purely quantum phenomenon is induced by the non-trivial reflection probability $(1-\tau)$ from 
the defect.

nodes.name: Current at nonzero mu_+
Current at mu_+ nonzero
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_1= \frac{\tau \mu_-}{2\pi} + \frac{\tau}{2\pi \beta} \ln \left [\frac{{\rm e}^{\beta \mu_{{}_+}}+{\rm e}^{-\beta \mu_{{}_-}}}{1+{\rm e}^{\beta(\mu_{{}_+}-\mu_{{}_-})}}\right ] \, .
nodes.label: si8

nodes.name: Parity of C_3 and C_4 in mu_-
nodes.statement:
It follows from (\ref{si3}) that for $\mu_+\not=0$ the cumulants $\mathcal C_3$ and 
$\mathcal C_4$ are respectively odd and even nonlinear functions of $\mu_-$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic slopes of C_3 and C_4
Asymptotic slopes of C_3, C_4
nodes.statement: \lim_{\mu_-\to \pm \infty} \frac{\mathcal C_3}{\mu_-} = \frac{\tau^2(\tau-1)}{\pi}\, ,\qquad \lim_{\mu_-\to \pm \infty} \frac{\mathcal C_4}{\mu_-} = \pm \frac{ \tau^2(\tau-1)(1-3\tau)}{\pi}\, ,
nodes.label: asymp

nodes.name: LLL minimal coupling
Minimal coupling
nodes.statement: {\rm i} \partial_x \longrightarrow {\rm i} \partial_x + A(x)\, .
nodes.label: minc1

LLL time-integrated correlator
nodes.statement: \int_0^T {\rm d} t_1\cdots \int_0^T {\rm d} t_n\, \langle j(t_1,x_1,i)\cdots j(t_1,x_1,i)\rangle_{\beta,\mu}
nodes.label: LL0

nodes.name: Levitov-Lee-Lesovik generating function
nodes.statement_short: For a delta-function counting potential, the LLL generating function at large T has transmission tau entering linearly.

nodes.name: Delta-function potential
nodes.statement: A(x) \sim \lambda\, \delta(x)
nodes.label: minc2

nodes.name: Levitov-Lee-Lesovik generating function
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_{L} (\lambda ) &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \ln \left [1+\frac{1}{2}(c_2+\tau c_1)\left ({\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda}-1\right ) + \frac{1}{2}(c_2-\tau c_1)\left ({\rm e}^{-{\rm i} \lambda}-1\right )\right ] \nonumber \\ &=&\int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \ln \left \{1+ {\rm i} c_1 \tau\, \sin (\lambda) + \tau c_2 \left [\cos (\lambda ) -1\right ]\right \} \, .
nodes.label: LL1

nodes.name: Coincidence of the two CGFs at tau=0,1
nodes.statement:
Nevertheless, comparing (\ref{gf4}) and (\ref{LL1}), we observe that these results coincide 
when the defect in the junction disconnects the leads ($\tau=0$), or when 
the defect is absent ($\tau=1$).

nodes.name: Coincidence of first two cumulants
nodes.statement:
Moreover, quite remarkably the first two 
cumulants generated by (\ref{gf4}) and (\ref{LL1}) coincide for any $\tau$.

nodes.name: Higher LLL cumulants differ in powers of tau
nodes.statement:
It turns out that they 
have the same monomials in $c_1$ and $c_2$, but with different 
powers of $\tau$. One has for instance 
\begin{eqnarray} 
\mathcal C_{L, 3} &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau c_1(1-3\tau c_2+2\tau c_1^2) \, , \\\
\mathcal C_{L, 4} &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau[c_2 -3\tau c_2^2+12\tau^2 c_1^2c_2 - 
2\tau c_1^2(2+3\tau^2 c_1^2)]\, , \end{eqnarray}
to be compared with (\ref{ec3},\ref{ec4}).

nodes.name: LLL third cumulant
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_{L, 3} &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau c_1(1-3\tau c_2+2\tau c_1^2) \, ,
nodes.label: LL2

nodes.name: LLL fourth cumulant
nodes.statement: \ \mathcal C_{L, 4} &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau[c_2 -3\tau c_2^2+12\tau^2 c_1^2c_2 - 2\tau c_1^2(2+3\tau^2 c_1^2)]\, ,
nodes.label: LL3

nodes.name: Single-channel moment generating function
nodes.statement:
In our case 
the moment generating function at fixed energy $\omega$ for the two-lead 
junction can be extracted from equation (\ref{C4}) in appendix C. One has 
\begin{equation}
\chi_\omega (\lambda) = 1+ {\rm i} c_1\sqrt{\tau}\, \sin \left (\lambda \sqrt{\tau }\right )+
c_2 \left [\cos \left (\lambda \sqrt{\tau} \right )-1\right ]\, , \end{equation} 
where $c_i(\omega)$ and $\tau(\omega)$ are given by (\ref{dc}-\ref{tr1}).

nodes.name: Moment generating function chi_omega
nodes.statement: \chi_\omega (\lambda) = 1+ {\rm i} c_1\sqrt{\tau}\, \sin \left (\lambda \sqrt{\tau }\right )+ c_2 \left [\cos \left (\lambda \sqrt{\tau} \right )-1\right ]\, ,
nodes.label: Mo0

nodes.name: Moments of the single-channel distribution
nodes.statement_short: Odd moments are c_1 tau^k and even moments c_2 tau^k.

nodes.name: Moment expansion
nodes.statement: \chi_\omega (\lambda) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{({\rm i} \lambda)^n}{n!}\, m_n
nodes.label: Mo1

nodes.name: Moment-cumulant consistency
nodes.statement:
One can verify that (\ref{Mo2}) and the cumulants at energy $\omega$, given by the integrands of 
(\ref{c51}, \ref{c52}) (see also (\ref{ec1}-\ref{ec6})), satisfy the conventional relations between 
moments and cumulants.

nodes.name: Moment problem for phi
nodes.statement_short: Find a probability density phi on a domain D whose moments are m_n.

nodes.name: Moment problem
nodes.statement: m_n = \int_{\cal D} {\rm d} \xi\, \xi^n \varphi (\xi)\, .
nodes.label: Mo3

nodes.name: Hamburger moment problem existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: A solution of the moment problem on the real line exists iff all Hankel determinants are non-negative.
conclusions:
A necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of 
$\varphi$ on $\mbox{${\mathbb R}$}$ is \cite{ST-70} the non-negativity of the Hankel determinants  
\begin{equation} 
\mathbb H_n \equiv 
\left | \begin{array}{cccccccc}
m_0&m_1&\cdots &&  m_n\\
m_1&m_2& \cdots & &m_{n+1}\\
\vdots &\vdots & \vdots&& \vdots \\
m_n&m_{n+1}& \cdots & &m_{2n}\\
\end{array}\right | \geq 0\, .
equivalent_conditions: the non-negativity of the Hankel determinants

nodes.name: Hankel determinants
nodes.statement: \mathbb H_n \equiv \left | \begin{array}{cccccccc} m_0&m_1&\cdots && m_n\\ m_1&m_2& \cdots & &m_{n+1}\\ \vdots &\vdots & \vdots&& \vdots \\ m_n&m_{n+1}& \cdots & &m_{2n}\\ \end{array}\right | \geq 0\, .
nodes.label: Mo4

nodes.name: Hankel determinants of the moments
Values of Hankel determinants
nodes.statement: \mathbb H_0 = 1\, , \qquad \mathbb H_1=\tau(c_2-c^2_1\tau)\, , \qquad \mathbb H_2=\tau^3(1-c_2)(c_2^2-c_1^2\tau)\, , \qquad \mathbb H_{n\geq 3} = 0\, .
nodes.label: Mo5

nodes.name: Non-negativity of the Hankel determinants
nodes.statement:
Using the explicit form of $c_i$ and that $\tau \in [0,1]$, 
one can show that $\mathbb H_2$ and $\mathbb H_3$ are non-negative.
nodes.statement_short: Use the explicit c_i and tau in [0,1] to show the Hankel determinants are non-negative, then apply the Hamburger criterion.

nodes.name: Existence of the distribution phi
nodes.statement:
Therefore the probability 
distribution $\varphi$ on $\mbox{${\mathbb R}$}$ exists.
conclusions:
Therefore the probability 
distribution $\varphi$ on $\mbox{${\mathbb R}$}$ exists.

nodes.name: Reduction to the Hamburger moment problem
Determinant H_2'
nodes.statement: \mathbb H_2^\prime \equiv \left | \begin{array}{cccccccc} m_1&m_2\\ m_2&m_3\\ \end{array}\right | = \tau^2 (c_1\tau -c_2) \leq 0\, ,
nodes.label: Mo4bis

nodes.name: phi supported at three points
nodes.statement:
Moreover, since $\mathbb H_{n\geq 3} = 0$ the  
general theory \cite{ST-70} implies that $\varphi$ 
is localised in three different points on the $\xi$-line.

nodes.name: Single-channel probability distribution
nodes.statement_short: phi is a sum of three delta functions at -e sqrt(tau), 0, e sqrt(tau) with weights (c_2 -+ c_1 sqrt(tau))/2 and 1-c_2.

nodes.name: Probability distribution phi
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \varphi (\xi) &= \int_{-\infty}^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \lambda}{2\pi}\, {\rm e}^{-{\rm i} \lambda \xi}\, \chi_\omega (\lambda ) \\ &=\frac{1}{2}(c_2-c_1\sqrt {\tau})\delta(\xi +e\sqrt {\tau})+(1-c_2) \delta(\xi) + \frac{1}{2}(c_2+c_1\sqrt {\tau})\delta(\xi -e \sqrt {\tau}) \, , \end{split}
nodes.label: Mo7

nodes.name: Normalisation of phi
Normalisation of phi
nodes.statement: \int_{-\infty}^\infty {\rm d} \xi\, \varphi (\xi) = 1
nodes.label: Mo8

nodes.name: Coefficients of phi are probabilities
nodes.statement:
One can show in addition that the coefficients of the delta 
distributions in (\ref{Mo7}) take value in the interval $[0,1]$ and have therefore 
a direct probabilistic interpretation.

nodes.name: Emission-absorption probability p_ij
nodes.statement:
The basic microscopic 
process, which takes place in the system for $\tau\not=0$, is the emission 
of a particle with energy $\omega$ from a reservoir 
$R_i$ and its absorption from $R_j$. Let us denote by $p_{ij}$ the relative 
probability.

nodes.name: Emission-absorption probabilities
nodes.statement:
Recalling that $\varphi$ concerns the lead $L_1$, the three terms in 
(\ref{Mo7}) correspond to the three elementary processes of emission and absorption 
relative to the reservoir $R_1$, namely: 

(i) $p_{12}=\frac{1}{2}(c_2-c_1\sqrt {\tau})$ is the probability for a particle to be 
emitted from $R_1$ and absorbed by $R_2$; 

(ii) $p_{11}=(1-c_2)$ is the probability for a particle to be emitted from and absorbed 
by $R_1$; 

(iii) $p_{21}=\frac{1}{2}(c_2+c_1\sqrt {\tau})$ is the probability for a particle 
to be emitted from $R_2$ and absorbed by $R_1$.
nodes.statement_short: The three weights of phi are p_12, p_11=1-c_2 and p_21.

nodes.name: Charge variation in each process
nodes.statement:
The variation $\xi$ of the charge in $L_1$, involved in these processes, is 
fixed by the support of the delta functions in (\ref{Mo7}) and is $\xi = e_{\rm eff}$, 
$\xi=0$ and $\xi=- e_{\rm eff}$ respectively, $e_{\rm eff}$ being defined in (\ref{si7}).

nodes.name: p_11 independent of tau
nodes.statement:
It is 
worth stressing that $p_{11}$ is $\tau$-independent as intuitively expected.

nodes.name: Distribution for disconnected leads
phi at tau=0
nodes.statement: \varphi (\xi)\vert_{\tau=0} = \delta(\xi)\, .
nodes.label: Mo7b

nodes.name: Discontinuity of p_ij at tau=0
nodes.statement:
The property (\ref{Mo7b}) implies also that as functions of $\tau$ the probabilities $p_{ij}$ 
are discontinuous at $\tau=0$, when the system divides in two parts.
conclusions:
as functions of $\tau$ the probabilities $p_{ij}$ 
are discontinuous at $\tau=0$

nodes.name: Distribution in lead L_2
nodes.statement:
The probability distribution $\varphi$ in $L_2$ is obtained by implementing $d_1 \leftrightarrow d_2$, 
or equivalently (see (\ref{dc})) by the substitutions $c_1 \to -c_1$ and $c_2 \to c_2$ in (\ref{Mo7}). 
As expected, under this operation one has $p_{12} \leftrightarrow p_{21}$. We deduce moreover  
that $p_{22}=p_{11}$, which completes the picture of the two lead junction at microscopic level.

nodes.name: Low-temperature limits of p_12 and p_21
Low-temperature limit of p_12
nodes.statement: \lim_{\beta \to \infty} p_{12}= \begin{cases} 0 \, , & \qquad \mu_+ < \omega-\mu_-\, , \\ (1-\sqrt{\tau})/2\, , & \qquad \omega -\mu_- < \mu_+ < \omega + \mu_-\, , \\ 0 \, , & \qquad \mu_+ > \omega+\mu_-\, , \\ \end{cases}
nodes.label: b2

nodes.name: Low-temperature limit of p_21
nodes.statement: \lim_{\beta \to \infty} p_{21}= \begin{cases} 0 \, , & \qquad \mu_+ < \omega-\mu_-\, , \\ (1+\sqrt{\tau})/2\, , & \qquad \omega -\mu_- < \mu_+ < \omega + \mu_-\, ,\\ 0 \, , & \qquad \mu_+ > \omega+\mu_-\, . \\ \end{cases}
nodes.label: b3

nodes.name: Limits at the boundary points
Boundary-point limits
nodes.statement: \lim_{\beta \to \infty} p_{12}&=&(1-\sqrt{\tau})/4\, ,\qquad \lim_{\beta \to \infty} p_{21}=(1+\sqrt{\tau})/4\, ,\qquad \mu_- \not= 0 \, , \nonumber \\ \lim_{\beta \to \infty} p_{12}&=& \lim_{\beta \to \infty} p_{21}= 1/4\, ,\qquad \mu_- = 0 \, .
nodes.label: b23

nodes.name: Dominant processes at low temperature
p_11 at the boundary points
nodes.statement:
Finally, equation (\ref{b23}) implies that in the low temperature limit 
$p_{11}=1/2$ for $\mu_+=\omega \pm \mu_-$.

nodes.name: High-temperature limit of p_12, p_21
High-energy limit of p_12, p_21
High-energy limit
nodes.statement: \lim_{\omega\to \infty} p_{12} = \lim_{\omega\to \infty} p_{21} =0\, ,
nodes.label: b5

nodes.name: CGF in terms of p_ij
Generating function via p_ij
nodes.statement: \mathcal C (\lambda ) &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \ln \left \{1+ {\rm i} (p_{21}-p_{12})\, \sin (\lambda \sqrt{\tau}) + (p_{21}+p_{12})\left [\cos (\lambda \sqrt{\tau})-1\right ] \right \} \nonumber \\ &=&\int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \ln \left [p_{11}+ p_{21}\, {\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda \sqrt{\tau}} + p_{12}\, {\rm e}^{-{\rm i} \lambda \sqrt{\tau}} \right ] \, .
nodes.label: gf4bis

nodes.name: Multi-terminal probability distribution
nodes.statement:
Second, the distribution (\ref{Mo7}) has a straightforward extension 
to the multi terminal system $N\geq 3$. In this case the probability distribution $\varphi (\xi)$ in the lead 
$L_1$ is obtained from (\ref{Mo7}) by replacing $c_i$ by the effective quantities $c_i^{\rm eff}$ 
according to (\ref{gf8}) and fixing $\tau$ by (\ref{gf7}). Now $p_{12}$ is the probability of 
the emission of a particle from $R_1$ and absorption by any of the reservoirs 
$\{R_2, R_3,...,R_N\}$, whereas $p_{21}$ gives the probability of the inverse process.

nodes.name: 2n-point function
nodes.statement: \langle a^*_{l_1}(k_1) a_{m_1}(p_1)\cdots a^*_{l_n}(k_n) a_{m_n}(p_n)\rangle_{\beta,\mu}

nodes.name: Gibbs expectation value
nodes.statement: \langle a^*_{l_1}(k_1) a_{m_1}(p_1)\cdots a^*_{l_n}(k_n) a_{m_n}(p_n)\rangle_{\beta,\mu} = \frac{1}{Z} {\rm Tr} \left [{\rm e}^{-K} a^*_{l_1}(k_1) a_{m_1}(p_1)\cdots a^*_{l_n}(k_n) a_{m_n}(p_n)\right ]\, ,
nodes.section: A Correlation functions in the LB state

nodes.name: Operator K and partition function Z
nodes.statement: K= \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} k}{2\pi} \sum_{i=1}^N \beta_i \left [\omega(k) - \mu_i\right ]a^*_i(k) a_i(k) \, , \quad Z = {\rm Tr} \left ({\rm e}^{-K}\right )\, .
nodes.section: A Correlation functions in the LB state
nodes.label: A3

nodes.name: Two-point functions
nodes.statement:
{}For the two-point functions one gets ($k>0,p>0$)
\begin{eqnarray} 
\langle a_l^*(k)a_m(p)\rangle_{\beta, \mu} &=& 
2\pi \delta (k-p)\delta_{lm}d_l[\omega(k)] \equiv \Delta_{lm}(k,p)\, , \\
\langle a_m(p) a_l^*(k)\rangle_{\beta, \mu} &=& 
2\pi \delta (k-p)\delta_{lm}\{1-d_l[\omega(k)]\} \equiv \widetilde{\Delta}_{lm}(k,p)\, , \end{eqnarray} 
where $d_l(\omega)$ is the Fermi distribution (\ref{c11}) of the reservoir $R_l$.
nodes.section: A Correlation functions in the LB state

nodes.name: Two-point function
nodes.statement: \langle a_l^*(k)a_m(p)\rangle_{\beta, \mu} &=& 2\pi \delta (k-p)\delta_{lm}d_l[\omega(k)] \equiv \Delta_{lm}(k,p)\, ,
nodes.section: A Correlation functions in the LB state
nodes.label: A4

nodes.name: Two-point function (reversed order)
nodes.statement: \langle a_m(p) a_l^*(k)\rangle_{\beta, \mu} &=& 2\pi \delta (k-p)\delta_{lm}\{1-d_l[\omega(k)]\} \equiv \widetilde{\Delta}_{lm}(k,p)\, ,
nodes.section: A Correlation functions in the LB state
nodes.label: A5

nodes.name: Determinant formula for the 2n-point function
nodes.statement:
The $2n$-point function can be expressed in terms of (\ref{A4},\ref{A5}) as a determinant. For  
$k_i>0,p_i>0$ one has:
\begin{eqnarray}
\langle a^*_{l_1}(k_1) a_{m_1}(p_1)\cdots a^*_{l_n}(k_n) a_{m_n}(p_n)\rangle_{\beta,\mu} = 
\qquad \qquad \quad  \nonumber \\
\left | \begin{array}{cccccccc}
\Delta_{l_1m_1}(k_1,p_1)&\Delta_{l_1m_2}(k_1,p_2)&\cdots &&  \Delta_{l_1m_n}(k_1,p_n)\\
-{\widetilde{\Delta}}_{l_2m_1}(k_2,p_1)&\Delta_{l_2m_2}(k_2,p_2) & \cdots & &\Delta_{l_2m_n}(k_2,p_n) \\
\vdots &\vdots & \vdots&& \vdots \\
-{\widetilde{\Delta}}_{l_nm_1}(k_n,p_1)&-{\widetilde{\Delta}}_{l_nm_2}(k_n,p_2) & \cdots & &\Delta_{l_nm_n}(k_n,p_n)\\
\end{array}\right | \, . \end{eqnarray}
